- **Workflow steps for displacement journey** (13 numbered steps):
  1. Provision Oyatie tenant + `web` + `commerce` + `marketing` + `apigw` + `developer-sdk` + `compliance` + `marketplace` µservices with Ghost-feature-parity (CMS + Members + Newsletters + Themes + Portal + Tips + Comments + Recommendations + Custom Integrations).
  2. Export Ghost Site via Admin API: site + posts + pages + tags + authors + members + tiers + subscriptions + newsletters + emails + tips + comments + recommendations + themes + integrations + webhooks + routes.yaml.
  3. Plan per-site migration cohorts.
  4. Per-Site: re-create with title + description + logo + brand-color + portal-settings + Stripe-status preserved.
  5. Per-Post + Page: re-create with Lexical-or-Mobiledoc → Oyatie rich-text transpile; SEO meta + canonical-URL preserved; visibility tier-binding preserved.
  6. Per-Tag + Author: re-create with visibility (public vs internal `#` prefix) preserved.
  7. Per-Member + Tier + Subscription: re-create with Stripe-subscription-ref + status + cadence preserved; Stripe-re-bind to Oyatie payment µservice.
  8. Per-Newsletter + Email: re-create with sender + branding + per-newsletter design; historical email-stats archived.
  9. Per-Tip + Comment + Recommendation: import with state preserved.
  10. Per-Theme: re-upload Handlebars-based theme; Routes.yaml transpile.
  11. Per-Integration + Webhook: re-create with API-key-pairs + HMAC-signed webhook URL re-register.
  12. Per-Members-Export: re-format CSV/JSON to Oyatie member-schema.
  13. Decommission Ghost per-site after 30-day shadow; DNS cutover; Ghost Pro contract sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Failure modes** (13 specific failures):
  - Lexical vs Mobiledoc AST drift (Ghost migrated from Mobiledoc to Lexical mid-2023; legacy posts may use Mobiledoc): per-post AST detect + transpile.
  - Card-type taxonomy in Lexical (HTML + bookmark + product + signup + email-only + button + gallery + video + audio + file + toggle + callout + header + divider + before-after + nft + market): per-card type-mapping preserve.
  - Members visibility filter NQL syntax (Ghost uses NQL — Notation Query Language for member filtering): per-filter NQL → Oyatie filter-DSL transpile.
  - Tier Stripe-Product-Ref re-bind during Stripe-migration: per-tier Stripe → Oyatie re-bind.
  - Internal-tag `#` prefix semantics: per-tag prefix preserve.
  - Newsletter per-tier delivery routing: per-newsletter tier-binding preserve.
  - Email recipient-filter NQL: per-email filter transpile.
  - Routes.yaml custom-routing DSL: per-site routes.yaml transpile + validation.
  - Handlebars theme template loop + helper + partial drift: per-theme template-tree transpile.
  - Portal modal embed snippet: per-site portal-snippet re-issue with new auth-endpoint.
  - Comments member-gated chain: per-comment member-gate preserve.
  - Recommendations cross-site one-click-subscribe re-register: per-recommendation network re-bind.
  - Members CSV/JSON export schema drift: per-export schema preserve + transpile.

- **Migration playbook outline** (10 numbered steps):
  1. Inventory via Ghost Admin API + Members-CSV-export.
  2. Plan 30-day shadow window with Stripe-re-bind scheduled.
  3. Migrate site + posts + pages + tags + authors with Lexical/Mobiledoc transpile.
  4. Migrate members + tiers + subscriptions + Stripe-re-bind.
  5. Migrate newsletters + emails + tips + comments + recommendations.
  6. Migrate themes + Routes.yaml + custom integrations + webhooks.
  7. Re-establish Portal modal embed snippet on existing pages.
  8. Re-establish SOC-2 / GDPR / PCI / CAN-SPAM / CASL attestations.
  9. Stripe-cutover from Ghost-to Oyatie payment-platform.
  10. Decommission Ghost per-site after 30-day shadow; DNS cutover; Ghost Pro sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Naming justification**: `web` + `commerce` + `marketing` + `apigw` + `developer-sdk` + `compliance` + `marketplace` are canonical 12-layer enum entries per ADR-0105 (13-value canonical); `ghost` + `ghost-pro` + `ghost-oss` + `ghost-members` + `ghost-newsletters` + `ghost-portal` + `ghost-tips` + `ghost-recommendations` + `ghost-comments` + `ghost-themes` + `ghost-routes-yaml` + `ghost-lexical` + `ghost-mobiledoc` + `ghost-sodo-search` are benchmark alias-only. The `web` µservice (per ADR-0131 per-microservice flat layout) is the canonical Ghost-equivalent publication + membership surface, distinct from the Substack-shape network-first newsletter (D-123) and Beehiiv-shape ad-monetized newsletter (D-124).

### Section D-151 - Cloudflare R2
- Vendor name and category: Cloudflare R2 (Cloudflare, Inc.) — S3-compatible object storage with zero egress fees: Buckets + Objects + Multipart Upload + Lifecycle Rules + Object Lock (governance + compliance modes) + Public Buckets + Custom Domains + CORS + Pre-signed URLs (V4 SigV4) + Event Notifications (to Queues) + R2 SQL (in development) + Super Slurper (S3/GCS migration) + R2 API (S3-compatible + Cloudflare-native) + Workers Bindings + Wrangler R2 commands + Storage Classes (Standard + Infrequent Access) + Location Hints (WNAM / ENAM / WEUR / EEUR / APAC) + Bucket-Level Tokens + Audit Log + Enterprise (SAML SSO + 99.99%-SLA + HIPAA-eligible + Dedicated Support).
- Coverage tier: A (capability fit on `storage` (Buckets + Objects + Multipart + Object-Lock + Lifecycle) + `apigw` (S3-compat REST + pre-signed URLs + custom domain) + `messaging` (Event Notifications to Queues) + `compliance` (SOC-2 + ISO + GDPR + HIPAA + Object-Lock WORM)). Capability-tier mapping per ADR-0316: Free (10 GB) → **Silver**; Paid → **Gold**; Enterprise (SAML + dedicated-support + 99.99%-SLA + HIPAA-BAA + object-lock-compliance + 100+ TB) → **Platinum**.
- Oyatie destination: `storage` (Buckets + Objects + Multipart + Object-Lock anchor); `apigw` (S3-compat REST + pre-signed URLs); `messaging` (Event-Notifications to Queues); `compliance` (SOC-2 + ISO + GDPR + HIPAA + WORM).

- **Vendor data model and top objects** (Cloudflare R2 canonical storage-graph):
  - `Account` (Account_ID, Name, Plan, SSO-Config).
  - `Bucket` (Bucket_ID, Account-Ref, Name, Location-Hint {wnam / enam / weur / eeur / apac / oc}, Storage-Class-Default {Standard / IA}, Public-Access, Custom-Domains[], CORS-Rules[], Lifecycle-Rules[], Object-Lock-Config, Event-Notifications[]).
  - `Object` (Object_ID, Bucket-Ref, Key, Size, ETag, ContentType, Metadata{User-Defined-K-V}, Storage-Class, Created-At, Modified-At, Version-ID, Object-Lock-Retain-Until-Date, Object-Lock-Mode {GOVERNANCE / COMPLIANCE}, Object-Lock-Legal-Hold).
  - `Multipart_Upload` (Upload_ID, Bucket-Ref, Key, Parts[Part-Number + ETag + Size]).
  - `Lifecycle_Rule` (Rule_ID, Bucket-Ref, Filter{Prefix + Tags[]}, Actions{Transition{Days + Storage-Class} + Expiration{Days + Date}}).
  - `CORS_Rule` (CORS_Rule_ID, Bucket-Ref, Allowed-Origins[], Allowed-Methods[], Allowed-Headers[], Max-Age).
  - `Object_Lock_Configuration` (Lock_Config_ID, Bucket-Ref, Default-Retention{Mode + Days/Years}, Object-Lock-Enabled).
  - `Pre_Signed_URL` (Signature, Expiry, Verb, Object-Ref).
  - `Custom_Domain` (Domain_ID, Bucket-Ref, Hostname, Cert-Status).
  - `Event_Notification` (Notif_ID, Bucket-Ref, Events[ObjectCreate + ObjectDelete], Target{Queue-Ref}).
  - `Bucket_Token` (Token_ID, Bucket-Ref, Permissions, Expiry).
  - `Super_Slurper_Job` (Job_ID, Account-Ref, Source{Type + Endpoint + Bucket + Creds}, Target-Bucket-Ref, Status, Progress).
  - `Audit_Event` (Event_ID, Actor-Ref, Bucket-Ref, Action).

- **Vendor primary APIs and endpoint shapes**:
  - S3-compatible: `https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/<bucket>/<key>` shapes `GET` + `PUT` + `DELETE` + `HEAD` + `LIST` + multipart (`POST ?uploads` + `PUT ?partNumber=N&uploadId=ID` + `POST ?uploadId=ID`).
  - Cloudflare-native REST: `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{id}/r2/buckets` shapes bucket + lifecycle + cors + object-lock + event-notifications + custom-domains.
  - Auth: SigV4 (Access-Key-ID + Secret) for S3; API Token for native REST.
  - CLI: `wrangler r2 bucket create` + `wrangler r2 object put/get/delete` + `wrangler r2 bucket lifecycle` + `wrangler r2 bucket cors`.
  - Workers Binding: `env.MY_BUCKET.get(key) / .put(key, value) / .delete(key) / .list()`.
  - Pre-signed URL: V4 SigV4 with expires + method + canonical-request.

- **Vendor distinctive UX surfaces**:
  - "Zero Egress Fees" — no charge for egress (free → caching CDN → web).
  - "S3-compatible API" — drop-in S3 SDK replacement.
  - "Object Lock (GOVERNANCE / COMPLIANCE)" — WORM retention.
  - "Lifecycle Rules" — transition + expiration.
  - "Custom Domains" — `objects.example.com` → bucket.
  - "Public Buckets + .r2.dev preview" — temporary public URL.
  - "Workers Bindings" — `env.MY_BUCKET` direct API in Worker.
  - "Wrangler R2 commands" — local CLI ops.
  - "Super Slurper" — one-shot S3/GCS → R2 migration.
  - "Location Hints" — WNAM / ENAM / WEUR / EEUR / APAC / OC.
  - "Event Notifications → Queues" — object-create / delete events.
  - "Bucket-Level Tokens" — scoped credential per bucket.
  - "Storage Classes (Standard + Infrequent Access)" — cost tier.
  - "Multipart Upload" — large-object resumable.

  ```
  permit(

    action in [

      Oyatie::Action::"R2ObjectPut", Oyatie::Action::"R2ObjectGet",

  ) when {
  ```

  - `r2.bucket` → `oya-storage-bucket` (location-hint + storage-class preserved).
  - `r2.object` → `oya-storage-object` (versioning + object-lock + storage-class preserved).
  - `r2.multipart_upload` → `oya-storage-multipart-upload`.
  - `r2.lifecycle_rule` → `oya-storage-lifecycle-rule` (transition + expiration preserved).
  - `r2.cors_rule` → `oya-apigw-cors-rule`.
  - `r2.object_lock_configuration` → `oya-compliance-worm-config` (GOVERNANCE / COMPLIANCE taxonomy preserved).
  - `r2.pre_signed_url` → `oya-apigw-pre-signed-url`.
  - `r2.custom_domain` → `oya-apigw-domain`.
  - `r2.event_notification` → `oya-messaging-event-notification`.
  - `r2.bucket_token` → `oya-identity-scoped-token`.
  - `r2.super_slurper_job` → `oya-storage-migration-job`.
  - `r2.audit_event` → `oya-compliance-audit-log-event`.

- **Workflow steps for displacement journey** (14 numbered steps):
  1. Provision Oyatie tenant + `storage` + `apigw` + `messaging` + `compliance` µservices with R2-feature-parity.
  2. Export R2 buckets + objects + multipart-uploads + lifecycle-rules + CORS + object-lock-config + custom-domains + event-notifications + bucket-tokens via S3-API + native REST.
  3. Plan per-bucket migration cohorts (group by location-hint + storage-class + lock-mode).
  4. Per-Bucket: re-create with location-hint + storage-class-default + lifecycle-rules + CORS + object-lock-config.
  5. Per-Object: replicate with key + size + ETag + content-type + metadata + storage-class + version-ID + lock-retain-until + lock-mode + legal-hold preserved.
  6. Per-Multipart-Upload (in-flight): complete or abort prior to migration cutover.
  7. Per-Lifecycle-Rule: transpile + golden-test on replicated tier.
  8. Per-CORS-Rule: transpile to Oyatie cors-rule preserving origins + methods + headers.
  9. Per-Object-Lock-Configuration: re-establish with mode (GOVERNANCE / COMPLIANCE) preserved; preserve retain-until + legal-hold.
  10. Per-Custom-Domain: re-register + DNS cutover; TLS continuity.
  11. Per-Event-Notification: re-wire to Oyatie messaging queue with object-create / delete events.
  12. Per-Bucket-Token: re-issue scoped credential.
  13. Per-Super-Slurper-Job: complete pending; re-establish if cross-cloud import ongoing.
  14. Decommission R2 per-bucket after 30-day shadow + lock-retention-respected sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Failure modes** (16 specific failures):
  - Object-Lock COMPLIANCE mode (irreversible) drift: migration cannot remove; per-object retain-until preserve.
  - Object-Lock GOVERNANCE mode bypass-permission semantics: per-bucket bypass-role preserve.
  - Pre-signed URL SigV4 algorithm drift: per-URL re-sign + grace window.
  - Lifecycle rule transition timing (days vs date): per-rule clock-anchor preserve.
  - CORS preflight semantics (allowed-origins + methods + headers + max-age): per-rule transpile + golden HTTP probe.
  - Multipart-upload part-numbering + max-parts (10000): per-upload parts-table preserve.
  - Custom-domain TLS cert renewal: per-domain ACME re-issue.
  - Event-notification at-least-once delivery semantics: per-notif policy preserve.
  - Bucket-token permissions taxonomy: per-token scope-mapping preserve.
  - Location-hint vs region-pin semantics (R2 hint vs Oyatie region): per-bucket region-mapping.
  - Storage-class transition (Standard ↔ IA): per-object class-replay.
  - Versioning enable/suspend per-bucket: per-bucket versioning-state preserve.
  - Etag computation (MD5 for single-PUT; multipart synthetic): per-object etag-recompute.
  - User-defined metadata case-sensitivity (`x-amz-meta-*`): per-object metadata-key normalize.
  - Public-bucket .r2.dev preview URL deprecation: per-bucket alias-map.
  - Audit Log retention (Enterprise 365-day): per-stream retention preserve.

- **Migration playbook outline** (10 numbered steps):
  1. Inventory via S3-API LIST + native REST + audit-log + Super-Slurper introspection.
  2. Plan 30-day shadow window with parallel writes.
  3. Migrate buckets + objects + multipart + lifecycle + CORS + object-lock.
  4. Migrate custom-domains + event-notifications + bucket-tokens + super-slurper-jobs.
  5. Re-establish public-bucket vs private-bucket semantics.
  6. Re-establish lifecycle + storage-class transitions on Oyatie tier.
  7. Re-establish event-notification → Oyatie messaging queue.
  8. Re-establish SOC-2 + ISO + GDPR + HIPAA + EU-DPF + SEC-17a-4 attestations.
  9. Cut DNS to Oyatie endpoint; preserve bucket-name + object-key + pre-signed-URL.
  10. Decommission R2 per-bucket after 30-day shadow + lock-retention-respected sunset; R2 sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Naming justification**: `storage` + `apigw` + `messaging` + `compliance` are canonical 12-layer enum entries per ADR-0105 (13-value canonical); `cloudflare-r2` + `r2-buckets` + `r2-objects` + `r2-object-lock` + `r2-lifecycle` + `r2-event-notifications` + `r2-super-slurper` + `r2-location-hints` are benchmark alias-only. The `storage` µservice (per ADR-0131 per-microservice flat layout) is the canonical R2-equivalent S3-compatible-object-storage surface.

### Section D-152 - MongoDB Atlas
- Vendor name and category: MongoDB Atlas (MongoDB, Inc.) — Multi-cloud managed MongoDB database-as-a-service: Atlas Clusters (M0..M700 + Serverless + Flex) + Replica Sets + Sharded Clusters + Atlas Search (Apache Lucene full-text + vector) + Atlas Vector Search + Atlas Data Federation + Atlas Data Lake + Atlas SQL Interface + Atlas Stream Processing + Atlas Triggers (Database + Auth + Scheduled) + Atlas Functions + Atlas App Services (formerly Realm) + Atlas Device Sync + Atlas Charts + Atlas Online Archive + Atlas Backup (Cloud + Continuous + PIT) + Atlas Encryption at Rest with KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault + Customer Managed Keys) + Atlas Client-Side Field Level Encryption + Atlas Queryable Encryption + Atlas Federated Authentication (SAML + OIDC) + Atlas API Keys (Project + Org) + Atlas Database Auditing + Atlas Performance Advisor + Atlas Network Peering (AWS PrivateLink + GCP Private Service + Azure Private Link) + Atlas IP Allowlist + Atlas BYOC + Atlas for Government (FedRAMP-Mod) + 100+ regions across AWS/GCP/Azure.
- Coverage tier: A (capability fit on `data` (clusters + replica sets + sharding + search + vector + federation + stream-processing) + `intelligence` (Vector Search + AI integrations) + `compute` (App Services + Functions + Triggers) + `apigw` (Data API + Atlas SQL) + `identity` (Federated Auth + SAML + OIDC) + `compliance` (SOC-2 + ISO + HIPAA + FedRAMP + PCI + GDPR + Queryable Encryption) + `observability` (Performance Advisor + Auditing)). Capability-tier mapping per ADR-0316: Free (M0) / Shared (M2-M5) → **Silver**; Dedicated (M10..M700) → **Gold**; Enterprise (BYOC + dedicated-VPC + CMK + HIPAA-BAA + FedRAMP-Mod + Queryable Encryption + dedicated-support + 99.995%-SLA) → **Platinum**.
- Oyatie destination: `data` (clusters + sharding + search + vector + federation + stream-processing anchor); `intelligence` (Vector Search); `compute` (App Services + Functions + Triggers); `apigw` (Data API); `identity` (Federated Auth); `compliance` (SOC-2 + ISO + HIPAA + FedRAMP + PCI + Queryable Encryption); `observability` (Performance Advisor + Auditing).

- **Vendor data model and top objects** (MongoDB Atlas canonical cluster-graph):
  - `Organization` (Org_ID, Name, Billing-Ref, Federation-Settings, API-Keys[]).
  - `Project` (Project_ID, Org-Ref, Name, Cluster-Settings, Network-Settings, Alert-Settings).
  - `Cluster` (Cluster_ID, Project-Ref, Name, Provider {AWS / GCP / Azure}, Region, Instance-Size {M0..M700 / Serverless / Flex}, MongoDB-Version, Disk-Size-GB, Replication-Spec{Num-Shards + Replication-Factor + Read-Only-Specs + Analytics-Specs}, Backup-Enabled, Encryption-At-Rest-Provider, Auto-Scaling, Paused).

  - `Vector_Index` (Vec_Index_ID, Coll-Ref, Path, Dimensions, Similarity {cosine / euclidean / dotProduct}, Quantization).
  - `Trigger` (Trigger_ID, App-Ref, Type {database / authentication / scheduled}, Function-Ref, Match-Expression / Cron-Expression).
  - `App_Services_App` (App_ID, Project-Ref, Name, Auth-Providers[Email + Anonymous + API-Key + JWT + Apple + Google + Facebook + Custom-Function + Custom-JWT], Functions[], GraphQL-Schema, Sync-Config).
  - `Function` (Fn_ID, App-Ref, Name, Source-Code, Run-As-User).

  - `Backup_Snapshot` (Snapshot_ID, Cluster-Ref, Created-At, Retention-Days, Compliance-Lock).

- **Vendor primary APIs and endpoint shapes**:
  - Atlas Admin REST API v2: `https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/` shapes `groups/{groupId}/clusters` + `groups/{groupId}/clusters/{name}/fts/indexes` + `groups/{groupId}/databaseUsers` + `groups/{groupId}/processArgs` + `groups/{groupId}/peers` + `groups/{groupId}/privateEndpoint` + `groups/{groupId}/customDBRoles` + `groups/{groupId}/maintenanceWindow` + `groups/{groupId}/backup/snapshots`.
  - Data API: `https://data.mongodb-api.com/app/{appId}/endpoint/data/v1` shapes `action/find` + `action/insertOne` + `action/updateOne` + `action/deleteOne` + `action/aggregate`.
  - MongoDB Wire Protocol: `mongodb+srv://<cluster>.mongodb.net/` (drivers: Node + Python + Java + Go + C# + Rust + Ruby + PHP + Scala + Kotlin + Swift).
  - Auth: Atlas API Key (Public + Private) + Programmatic API Keys (Org + Project) + Database User credentials.
  - CLI: `atlas` (Atlas CLI) + `mongosh` + `mongodump` + `mongorestore` + `mongoimport` + `mongoexport`.

- **Vendor distinctive UX surfaces**:
  - "Cluster Builder" — multi-cloud + multi-region picker.
  - "Atlas Search" — Lucene full-text with custom analyzers.
  - "Atlas Vector Search" — managed vector index with $vectorSearch aggregation.
  - "Performance Advisor" — index suggestions + slow query analyzer.
  - "Data Explorer" — in-browser collection browser with CRUD.
  - "Charts" — embedded BI / dashboard.
  - "App Services Console" — Functions + Triggers + GraphQL + Device Sync.
  - "Stream Processing UI" — pipeline-builder (sources + windowing + sinks).
  - "Online Archive Setup" — TTL-based offload to cold storage.
  - "Backup Restore" — snapshot + point-in-time + queryable.
  - "Network Peering Wizard" — AWS/GCP/Azure VPC peering + PrivateLink.
  - "Encryption Key Management" — KMS provider linking + key rotation.
  - "Database Access" — DB-User + Role-Builder.
  - "Audit Filter Builder" — JSON filter + format picker.

- **Cedar permit shape** (data + intelligence + compute + apigw + identity + compliance + observability):
  ```
  permit(
    principal == Oyatie::User::"<atlas-user-id>",
    action in [
      Oyatie::Action::"AtlasClusterCreate", Oyatie::Action::"AtlasClusterScale",
      Oyatie::Action::"AtlasClusterDelete", Oyatie::Action::"AtlasClusterPause",
      Oyatie::Action::"AtlasClusterResume", Oyatie::Action::"AtlasDatabaseCreate",
      Oyatie::Action::"AtlasCollectionCreate", Oyatie::Action::"AtlasIndexCreate",
      Oyatie::Action::"AtlasSearchIndexCreate", Oyatie::Action::"AtlasVectorIndexCreate",
      Oyatie::Action::"AtlasTriggerCreate", Oyatie::Action::"AtlasFunctionDeploy",
      Oyatie::Action::"AtlasDataAPIInvoke", Oyatie::Action::"AtlasOnlineArchiveConfig",
      Oyatie::Action::"AtlasBackupSnapshotRestore", Oyatie::Action::"AtlasStreamProcessorStart",
      Oyatie::Action::"AtlasNetworkPeeringCreate", Oyatie::Action::"AtlasPrivateEndpointCreate",
      Oyatie::Action::"AtlasIPAllowlistEdit", Oyatie::Action::"AtlasDatabaseUserCreate",
      Oyatie::Action::"AtlasEncryptionKeyLink", Oyatie::Action::"AtlasAuditFilterSet",
      Oyatie::Action::"AtlasFederationConfig", Oyatie::Action::"AtlasAuditLogExport"
    ],
    resource in [
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasOrg::"<org-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasProject::"<proj-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasCluster::"<cluster-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasDatabase::"<db-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasCollection::"<coll-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasSearchIndex::"<idx-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasVectorIndex::"<vec-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasTrigger::"<trigger-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasAppServicesApp::"<app-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasFunction::"<fn-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasOnlineArchive::"<archive-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasBackupSnapshot::"<snap-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasStreamProcessor::"<sp-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasNetworkPeering::"<peer-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasPrivateEndpoint::"<pe-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasDatabaseUser::"<dbu-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasEncryptionKey::"<key-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::AtlasAuditLogStream::"<stream-id>"
    ]
  ) when {
    resource.tenant == principal.tenant &&
    principal.role in resource.allowed_roles &&
    (resource.kind != "cluster_delete" || (principal.role in ["project_owner", "org_owner"] && context.dual_control_approver_present == true && context.cluster_data_export_complete == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "backup_snapshot_restore_to_production" || (principal.role in ["project_owner", "db_admin"] && context.change_window_open == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "network_peering_create_production_vpc" || principal.role in ["project_owner", "network_admin"]) &&
    (resource.kind != "ip_allowlist_edit_open_world" || false) &&
    (resource.kind != "database_user_create_admin_role" || (principal.role in ["project_owner"] && context.dual_control_approver_present == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "encryption_key_link_cmk" || (principal.role in ["project_owner", "security_admin"] && context.kms_test_decrypt_ok == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "data_api_invoke_pii" || (context.pii_workspace_optin == true && context.tenant_data_classification_pii == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "online_archive_config_legal_hold_data" || principal.role in ["governance_admin"]) &&
    (resource.kind != "vector_index_create_eu_pii" || (context.eu_region_pin == true && context.tenant_ai_optin == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "federation_config_change" || (principal.role == "org_owner" && context.dual_control_approver_present == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "audit_log_export" || principal.role in ["compliance_admin", "org_owner"])
  };
  ```
  Per-jurisdiction packs: SOC-2 Type II; ISO-27001 + ISO-27017 + ISO-27018; GDPR + EU-DPF + KR-PIPA; HIPAA-BAA (BAA-eligible); FedRAMP-Moderate (Atlas for Government); PCI-DSS Level 1; CSA STAR; Queryable Encryption per FIPS 140-3 module.

- **Ontology projection**:
  - `atlas.organization` + `atlas.project` → `oya-identity-org` + `-project`.
  - `atlas.cluster` → `oya-data-document-cluster` (provider + region + shape + instance-size + replication-spec preserved).
  - `atlas.database` + `atlas.collection` → `oya-data-document-db` + `-collection` (validators + shard-key + capped + TTL preserved).
  - `atlas.search_index` + `atlas.vector_index` → `oya-data-search-index` + `oya-intelligence-vector-index`.
  - `atlas.trigger` → `oya-compute-trigger` (database / auth / scheduled taxonomy preserved).

  - `atlas.online_archive` → `oya-storage-archive-policy`.
  - `atlas.backup_snapshot` → `oya-data-backup-snapshot` (compliance-lock preserved).
  - `atlas.stream_processor` → `oya-data-stream-processor`.

  - `atlas.ip_allowlist_entry` → `oya-network-ip-allowlist-entry`.
  - `atlas.database_user` → `oya-identity-db-user` (5-auth-type taxonomy preserved).
  - `atlas.encryption_key` → `oya-compliance-cmk-binding`.
  - `atlas.audit_filter` → `oya-compliance-audit-filter`.

- **Workflow steps for displacement journey** (16 numbered steps):
  1. Provision Oyatie tenant + `data` + `intelligence` + `compute` + `apigw` + `identity` + `compliance` + `observability` µservices with Atlas-feature-parity.
  2. Export Atlas org + projects + clusters + DBs + collections + indexes + search/vector indexes + triggers + functions + apps + archives + backups + stream-processors + network-peering + private-endpoints + IP-allowlists + DB-users + encryption-keys + audit-filters via Admin API v2.
  3. Plan per-project migration cohorts (group by provider + region + workload).
  4. Per-Project: re-create with cluster-settings + network-settings + alert-settings.
  5. Per-Cluster: re-provision with provider + region + instance-size + replication-spec + backup + encryption + auto-scaling preserved.
  6. Per-Database + Collection: replicate with validators + shard-key + capped + TTL preserved (mongodump + mongorestore + change-stream tail).
  7. Per-Search-Index: re-create with Lucene mappings + analyzers + similarity preserved.
  8. Per-Vector-Index: re-create with path + dimensions + similarity + quantization preserved; re-embed and verify recall.
  9. Per-Trigger: re-create with type + function-ref + match-expression / cron preserved.
  10. Per-App-Services-App + Function: redeploy with auth-providers + GraphQL-schema + sync-config preserved.
  11. Per-Data-Federation + Online-Archive: re-establish storage links + criteria; preserve compliance-lock for archived data.
  12. Per-Stream-Processor: transpile pipeline (source + window + sink).
  13. Per-Network-Peering + Private-Endpoint: re-establish to Oyatie equivalents (VPC peering / PrivateLink / Private Service / Private Link).
  14. Per-IP-Allowlist + DB-User: re-issue with auth-type + roles preserved.
  15. Per-Encryption-Key: re-link KMS CMK; rotate; re-encrypt where required; preserve queryable-encryption keys per ADR-0251 §D-10.
  16. Decommission Atlas per-project after 30-day shadow + change-stream cutover; Atlas sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Failure modes** (17 specific failures):
  - Wire protocol parity (OP_MSG + change streams + sessions + retryable writes + transactions): per-driver compatibility test.
  - Sharding key + chunk distribution preservation: per-collection shard-rebalance.
  - Replica-set read preference (primary / primaryPreferred / secondary / secondaryPreferred / nearest): per-client preference preserve.
  - Aggregation pipeline + $vectorSearch + $search semantics: per-pipeline golden-test.
  - Search analyzer custom char/token filters: per-index analyzer transpile.
  - Vector quantization (scalar / binary) + ANN recall: per-index recall replay.
  - Change-stream resume tokens: per-consumer resume-state preserve.
  - Online Archive TTL semantics + compliance-lock: per-archive lock preserve.
  - Continuous backup + PIT-restore RPO/RTO: per-cluster backup-policy preserve.
  - Queryable Encryption (deterministic + range) key bundle: per-field key migration.
  - Client-Side Field Level Encryption schema + KMS provider: per-collection schema migration.
  - FedRAMP-Moderate boundary (Atlas for Government enclave): per-cluster boundary preserve.
  - HIPAA-BAA scope (PHI workload tagging): per-project PHI flag preserve.
  - PrivateLink endpoint-service-name drift across providers: per-endpoint re-bind.
  - Triggers ordering + retry semantics + dead-letter: per-trigger DLQ + retry-policy preserve.
  - App Services Device Sync conflict resolution rules: per-sync-set rules preserve.
  - Audit filter format (BSON / JSON) + destination (syslog / file): per-filter format-mapping.

- **Migration playbook outline** (10 numbered steps):
  1. Inventory via Atlas Admin API + CLI + audit-stream.
  2. Plan 30-day shadow window with change-stream parallel writes.
  3. Migrate clusters + DBs + collections + indexes + search + vector indexes.
  4. Migrate triggers + functions + app-services + data-federation + online-archive + backup-snapshots + stream-processors.
  5. Re-establish network-peering + private-endpoints + IP-allowlists + DB-users + encryption-keys.
  6. Re-establish federated-auth + audit-filters.
  7. Re-establish HIPAA + FedRAMP-Mod + PCI-DSS + SOC-2 + ISO + GDPR + EU-DPF + KR-PIPA attestations.
  8. Re-establish Queryable Encryption keys + CSFLE schemas.
  9. Cut connection strings + DNS to Oyatie endpoint; preserve `mongodb+srv://` alias.
  10. Decommission Atlas per-project after 30-day shadow + compliance-lock-respected sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Naming justification**: `data` + `intelligence` + `compute` + `apigw` + `identity` + `compliance` + `observability` are canonical 12-layer enum entries per ADR-0105 (13-value canonical); `mongodb-atlas` + `atlas-clusters` + `atlas-search` + `atlas-vector-search` + `atlas-app-services` + `atlas-functions` + `atlas-triggers` + `atlas-data-federation` + `atlas-online-archive` + `atlas-stream-processing` + `atlas-private-link` + `atlas-cmk` + `atlas-queryable-encryption` + `atlas-for-government` are benchmark alias-only. The `data` µservice (per ADR-0131 per-microservice flat layout) is the canonical MongoDB-Atlas-equivalent multi-cloud document-DB-as-a-service surface.

### Section D-153 - Confluent Cloud
- Vendor name and category: Confluent Cloud (Confluent, Inc.) — Fully managed Apache Kafka platform: Kafka clusters (Basic + Standard + Dedicated + Enterprise + Freight) + Schema Registry + ksqlDB + Flink (managed Apache Flink) + (200+ source/sink connectors via Confluent Hub) + Cluster Linking (geo-replication) + Stream Governance (data lineage + catalog + quality) + Stream Sharing + Tableflow (Kafka → Iceberg) + Confluent CLI + Terraform provider + REST API v3 + Kafka REST Proxy + multi-cloud (AWS / GCP / Azure) + 70+ regions + Private Networking (VPC Peering + PrivateLink + Transit Gateway) + BYOK / Customer Managed Keys + SSO (SAML + OIDC) + Group Mappings + Audit Log (RBAC + Authentication + Authorization) + 99.99% SLA (Dedicated/Enterprise).
- Coverage tier: A (capability fit on `messaging` (Kafka clusters + topics + partitions + producers + consumers) + `data` (Schema Registry + ksqlDB + Flink + Tableflow → Iceberg) + `developer-experience` (+ Terraform + CLI) + `apigw` (REST Proxy + Stream Sharing) + `network` (VPC peering + PrivateLink + Transit Gateway) + `identity` (SSO + RBAC + group mappings) + `compliance` (SOC-2 + ISO + HIPAA + PCI + GDPR + BYOK)). Capability-tier mapping per ADR-0316: Basic → **Silver**; Standard → **Gold**; Dedicated / Enterprise / Freight (BYOK + PrivateLink + dedicated-network + HIPAA-BAA + 99.99%-SLA + FedRAMP path) → **Platinum**.
- Oyatie destination: `messaging` (Kafka clusters + topics anchor); `data` (Schema Registry + ksqlDB + Flink + Tableflow); `developer-experience` (+ Terraform); `apigw` (REST Proxy); `network` (peering + PrivateLink); `identity` (SSO + RBAC); `compliance` (SOC-2 + ISO + HIPAA + PCI + BYOK).

- **Vendor data model and top objects** (Confluent Cloud canonical streaming-graph):
  - `Organization` (Org_ID, Name, Billing-Ref, SSO-Config, Group-Mappings[]).
  - `Environment` (Env_ID, Org-Ref, Name, Stream-Governance-Package {Essentials / Advanced}).

  - `Schema_Registry` (SR_ID, Env-Ref, Provider, Region, Compatibility-Default {Backward / Forward / Full / None / + variants}).

  - `Connector` (Connector_ID, Cluster-Ref, Plugin-Class, Config{topic + tasks.max + transforms + producer overrides + consumer overrides}, Status).
  - `ksqlDB_Cluster` (ksql_ID, Env-Ref, Cluster-Ref, CSU {ksqlDB Streaming Units}, Persistent-Queries[]).
  - `Flink_Compute_Pool` (Pool_ID, Env-Ref, Region, Max-CFU {Confluent Flink Units}, Statement-Defaults).
  - `Flink_Statement` (Stmt_ID, Pool-Ref, Name, SQL, Status, Properties).
  - `Cluster_Link` (Link_ID, Source-Cluster-Ref, Dest-Cluster-Ref, Direction {source-initiated / destination-initiated}, Mirror-Topics[], Filters[]).
  - `Stream_Share` (Share_ID, Provider-Topic-Ref, Consumer-Org-Ref, Status).
  - `Tableflow_Table` (Tableflow_ID, Topic-Ref, Target {Apache Iceberg + Delta Lake roadmap}, Storage{S3 + GCS + Azure-Blob}, Schema-Mode).
  - `Network` (Network_ID, Env-Ref, Provider, Region, Connection-Type {peering / privatelink / transit-gateway}, CIDR).
  - `Audit_Log_Sink` (Audit_ID, Org-Ref, Destination-Cluster-Ref).
  - `Encryption_Key` (Key_ID, Env-Ref, KMS-Provider, CMK-ARN).
  - `Stream_Catalog_Entity` (Entity_ID, Type {Topic / Schema / Field / Connector}, Tags[], Business-Metadata).

- **Vendor primary APIs and endpoint shapes**:
  - Confluent Cloud REST v3: `https://api.confluent.cloud/` shapes `/cmk/v2/clusters` + `/iam/v2/service-accounts` + `/iam/v2/api-keys` + `/srcm/v2/clusters` + `/kafka-quotas/v1/client-quotas` + `/connect/v1/environments/{env}/clusters/{cluster}/connectors` + `/networking/v1/networks` + `/networking/v1/private-link-attachments` + `/billing/v1/costs`.
  - Kafka REST Proxy: `https://<cluster>.confluent.cloud/kafka/v3/clusters/{cluster_id}/topics` + records.
  - Kafka protocol: bootstrap.servers `<broker>.confluent.cloud:9092` + SASL/PLAIN + SSL.
  - ksqlDB API: `https://<ksql>.confluent.cloud/ksql` + `/query` + `/info` + `/healthcheck`.
  - Flink SQL API: REST endpoint for compute pool + statements.
  - Schema Registry: `https://<sr>.confluent.cloud/subjects/{subject}/versions` + `/schemas/ids/{id}` + `/compatibility/subjects/{subject}/versions/{version}` + `/config/{subject}`.
  - CLI: `confluent` (login + kafka cluster + kafka topic + kafka acl + iam + connect cluster + ksql + flink + schema-registry + tableflow + network + audit-log + price + service-account + api-key).
  - Terraform provider: `confluentinc/confluent` (`confluent_cluster` + `confluent_topic` + `confluent_acl` + `confluent_schema` + `confluent_connector` + `confluent_ksql_cluster` + `confluent_flink_compute_pool` + `confluent_cluster_link` + `confluent_tableflow_topic` + `confluent_network` + `confluent_private_link_attachment` + `confluent_byok_key`).

- **Vendor distinctive UX surfaces**:
  - "Cloud Console" — environment + cluster + topic + connector + ksqlDB + Flink + Schema Registry tabs.
  - "Topic Messages Viewer" — sample messages with schema decoding.
  - "Stream Lineage" — visual end-to-end flow (producers + topics + consumers + connectors + streams).
  - "Stream Catalog" — searchable catalog of topics + schemas + tags + business-metadata.
  - "Stream Quality" — rule-based + statistical quality monitoring.
  - "Plugin Marketplace" — 200+ connectors with self-managed + fully-managed lanes.
  - "ksqlDB Editor" — SQL-style stream + table queries.
  - "Flink SQL Workspace" — managed-Flink statement editor + compute-pool picker.
  - "Cluster Linking" — geo-replication with mirror topics + filter rules.
  - "Stream Sharing" — sharable topics across orgs (consumer-pull).
  - "Tableflow" — topics-as-Iceberg-tables for analytics.
  - "Network Wizard" — peering / PrivateLink / Transit-Gateway setup.
  - "RBAC Page" — role bindings on org / env / cluster / topic / subject scopes.
  - "Audit Log Sink" — central destination cluster for audit events.
  - "Cost Page" — cluster + connector + ksqlDB + Flink unit-cost breakdown.

  ```
    (resource.kind != "schema_compatibility_change_to_none" || (principal.role in ["env_admin", "governance_admin"] && context.dual_control_approver_present == true)) &&
  ```

- **Ontology projection**:
  - `confluent.organization` + `confluent.environment` → `oya-identity-org` + `oya-messaging-environment`.
  - `confluent.cluster` → `oya-messaging-kafka-cluster` (5-type taxonomy + CKU sizing preserved).
  - `confluent.topic` → `oya-messaging-topic` (partition + replication + retention preserved).
  - `confluent.acl` → `oya-messaging-acl` (resource-type + pattern-type + operation taxonomy preserved).
  - `confluent.service_account` + `confluent.api_key` → `oya-identity-service-account` + `oya-identity-api-key`.
  - `confluent.schema_registry` + `confluent.schema` → `oya-data-schema-registry` + `oya-data-schema` (AVRO / JSON / PROTOBUF taxonomy preserved).
  - `confluent.connector` → `oya-data-connector` (plugin-class taxonomy preserved).
  - `confluent.ksqldb_cluster` → `oya-data-stream-processor-ksqldb`.
  - `confluent.flink_compute_pool` + `confluent.flink_statement` → `oya-data-flink-pool` + `-statement`.
  - `confluent.cluster_link` → `oya-messaging-cluster-link` (direction taxonomy preserved).
  - `confluent.stream_share` → `oya-messaging-topic-share`.
  - `confluent.tableflow_table` → `oya-data-tableflow-table` (Iceberg target preserved).
  - `confluent.network` + `confluent.private_link_attachment` → `oya-network-peering` + `oya-network-private-endpoint`.
  - `confluent.audit_log_sink` → `oya-compliance-audit-log-sink`.
  - `confluent.encryption_key` → `oya-compliance-cmk-binding`.
  - `confluent.stream_catalog_entity` → `oya-data-catalog-entity`.

- **Workflow steps for displacement journey** (17 numbered steps):
  1. Provision Oyatie tenant + `messaging` + `data` + `developer-experience` + `apigw` + `network` + `identity` + `compliance` µservices with Confluent-feature-parity.
  2. Export Confluent org + envs + clusters + topics + ACLs + service-accounts + API-keys + schema-registries + schemas + connectors + ksqlDB + Flink + cluster-links + stream-shares + tableflow + networks + audit-sinks via REST v3 + CLI.
  3. Plan per-cluster migration cohorts (group by provider + region + workload).
  4. Per-Env: re-create with stream-governance-package preserved.
  5. Per-Cluster: re-provision with type + provider + region + network + CKU + availability + encryption-mode preserved.
  6. Per-Topic: re-create with partitions + replication-factor + configs preserved; replicate via MirrorMaker2 / Cluster Linking.
  7. Per-ACL: re-create with principal + resource-type + pattern-type + operation + permission preserved.
  8. Per-Service-Account + API-Key: re-issue; rotate secrets.
  9. Per-Schema-Registry + Schema: replicate with subject + version + compatibility preserved.
  10. Per-Connector: redeploy with plugin-class + config preserved; offset commit replay.
  11. Per-ksqlDB-Cluster + Persistent-Queries: re-instantiate.
  12. Per-Flink-Compute-Pool + Statement: re-instantiate with SQL + properties preserved.
  13. Per-Cluster-Link: re-establish with direction + mirror-topics + filters preserved.
  14. Per-Stream-Share: re-grant consumer-org access.
  15. Per-Tableflow-Table: re-instantiate with Iceberg target preserved.
  16. Per-Network + PrivateLink + BYOK + Audit-Sink: re-establish.
  17. Decommission Confluent per-cluster after 30-day shadow + consumer-lag-zero + offset-cutover; Confluent sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Failure modes** (18 specific failures):
  - Topic config drift (retention.ms / cleanup.policy / compression / min.insync.replicas): per-topic config snapshot + compare.
  - Partition count cannot decrease post-create: per-topic partition-bump plan.
  - Consumer-group offset preservation across cluster link cutover: per-group offset translation.
  - Schema compatibility (Backward / Forward / Full / None + Transitive variants): per-subject compatibility preserve.
  - Schema reference graph (subject A references subject B): per-subject DAG migrate-in-order.
  - offsets + per-task progress: per-connector offset replay.
  - ksqlDB persistent-query state-store: per-query state migrate or rebuild.
  - Flink statement savepoint / checkpoint: per-statement savepoint restore.
  - Cluster Linking direction (source-initiated vs destination-initiated): per-link direction preserve.
  - Mirror-topic name transformation rules: per-link rename-policy preserve.
  - Exactly-once-semantics (idempotent producer + transactional.id): per-producer EOS preserve.
  - SASL/PLAIN credential rotation without consumer outage: per-cluster API-key dual-key rotation.
  - BYOK CMK key-policy + grants: per-cluster key-policy migrate.
  - PrivateLink endpoint-service drift across AWS / GCP / Azure: per-attachment re-bind.
  - Stream-share consumer-pull semantics + auth: per-share token re-issue.
  - Tableflow Iceberg snapshot semantics: per-table snapshot-id preserve.
  - Audit log destination ordering + retention: per-sink retention preserve.
  - Stream-governance catalog tags + business-metadata: per-entity tag-map preserve.

- **Migration playbook outline** (10 numbered steps):
  1. Inventory via Confluent REST v3 + CLI + Terraform state.
  2. Plan 30-day shadow with MirrorMaker2 / Cluster Linking dual-write.
  3. Migrate clusters + topics + ACLs + service-accounts + API-keys.
  4. Migrate schema-registries + schemas + connectors + ksqlDB + Flink + cluster-links.
  5. Migrate stream-shares + tableflow + networks + private-link + BYOK + audit-sinks.
  6. Re-establish exactly-once-semantics + producer/consumer config.
  7. Re-establish SSO + RBAC + group-mappings.
  8. Re-establish SOC-2 + ISO + HIPAA + PCI + GDPR + EU-DPF + KR-PIPA attestations.
  9. Cut bootstrap.servers + DNS to Oyatie endpoint; preserve cluster bootstrap alias.
  10. Decommission Confluent per-cluster after 30-day shadow + offset-zero sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Naming justification**: `messaging` + `data` + `developer-experience` + `apigw` + `network` + `identity` + `compliance` are canonical 12-layer enum entries per ADR-0105 (13-value canonical); `confluent-cloud` + `confluent-cluster` + `confluent-topic` + `confluent-acl` + `confluent-schema-registry` + `confluent-connect` + `confluent-ksqldb` + `confluent-flink` + `confluent-cluster-link` + `confluent-stream-share` + `confluent-tableflow` + `confluent-private-link` + `confluent-byok` + `confluent-stream-governance` + `confluent-stream-catalog` + `confluent-stream-quality` + `confluent-stream-lineage` are benchmark alias-only. The `messaging` µservice (per ADR-0131 per-microservice flat layout) is the canonical Confluent-Cloud-equivalent fully-managed-Kafka surface.

(See §27 of `docs/architecture/wave-3-g-synthesis-adjudication-2026-05-21.md` for synthesis-audit-blessed pattern.)

### Section D-123 - Substack
- Vendor name and category: Substack Inc. — Substack publishing + paid-subscription network: Substack Newsletters (writer-first email publication + web-archive + RSS) + Paid Subscriptions (Stripe Standard + monthly + annual + founding-member tier + comp + free-trial) + Substack Network (cross-publication recommendations + subscribe-to-other-newsletters + reader Inbox + Notes) + Substack Notes (Twitter-like microblog feed) + Substack Chat (publication chat — like Discord channels for paid subscribers) + Substack Podcast (audio episodes + transcripts + RSS-feed) + Substack Video (video episodes) + Substack Threads + Substack Comments + Substack Discussion Threads + Substack Polls + Reader App (iOS + Android) + Web reader + Email delivery (DKIM + DMARC + SPF + Amazon SES) + Custom Domains + Substack Pro (advances + grants for top writers) + Substack Bestsellers (badge program) + Substack Reads (curated discovery) + Substack Leaderboards + Substack Stats (subscriber + revenue + open/click) + Imports (Mailchimp + Beehiiv + ConvertKit + Ghost + WordPress + CSV) + Exports (CSV + Stripe-Subscription-export) + Stripe Standard payments + Founding Member badge + Bestseller badges (Hundreds / Thousands / Tens-of-Thousands / Hundreds-of-Thousands / Millions).
- Coverage tier: A (capability fit on `web` (publication anchor — Substack differentiated by network-first cross-publication discovery + paid-subscription as core primitive + Notes microblog + Chat) + `commerce` (paid subscriptions + founding-member + Stripe Standard) + `marketing` (Email delivery + Notes + Recommendations + Bestsellers + Network) + `collaboration` (Comments + Chat + Discussion Threads + Polls) + `apigw` (Substack does NOT expose a public REST API — limited Reader-feed-RSS + UI-driven flows; this is a key constraint) + `compliance` (GDPR + CCPA + CAN-SPAM + CASL + PCI-DSS via Stripe + EU-DPF)). Capability-tier mapping per ADR-0316: Free (writer-side; Substack takes 10% of paid revenue) → **Silver**; Substack-Pro (advances/grants for select writers) → **Gold**; Substack-Bestseller-Status writers (≥1000 paid subs with revenue scale + Pro support + dedicated CSM) → **Platinum**.
- Oyatie destination: `web` (publication + newsletter + post anchor); `commerce` (paid subscriptions + Stripe Connect); `marketing` (Notes + Recommendations + Bestsellers + cross-network); `collaboration` (Comments + Chat + Threads); `apigw` (limited — Substack import + export adapter, no public REST API by design); `compliance` (GDPR + CCPA + CAN-SPAM + PCI).

- **Vendor data model and top objects** (Substack canonical publication-network model):
  - `Publication` (Publication_ID, Name, Subdomain, Custom-Domain, Description, Logo, Cover-Image, About-Page, Author-Refs[], Editor-Refs[], Plan-Stripe-Refs[], Founding-Member-Plan, Email-Sender-Name, Reply-To, Time-Zone, Locale, Created-At).
  - `Author` (Author_ID, Email, Name, Bio, Photo, Substack-Pro-Member, Bestseller-Badge-Level {0 / 100s / 1000s / 10000s / 100000s / 1M+}, Writing-On-Substack-Since, Earnings-Lifetime).
  - `Post` (Post_ID, Publication-Ref, Title, Subtitle, Slug, Body-HTML, Body-Plaintext, Type {newsletter / podcast / video / discussion_thread / chat_pin / note}, Audience {everyone / paid / founding}, Send-Email, Sent-Status, Send-Time, Scheduled-Time, Publish-Time, Featured, Cover-Image, Audio-Items[], Video-Items[], Tags[], Section-Ref).
  - `Section` (Section_ID, Publication-Ref, Name, Slug, Description, Order, Visibility {public / paid}).
  - `Subscriber` (Subscriber_ID, Publication-Ref, Email, Name, Status {free / paid / comp / founding / cancelled}, Source {direct / cross_recommend / imported / network}, Subscription-Stripe-Ref, Plan-Ref, Monthly-or-Annual, Created-At, Paying-Since, Lifetime-Revenue, Open-Rate, Click-Rate).
  - `Subscription_Plan` (Plan_ID, Publication-Ref, Type {monthly / annual / founding / comp}, Price, Currency, Stripe-Product-Ref, Founding-Tier-Suggested-Amount, Trial-Period-Days).

  - `Note` (Note_ID, Author-Ref, Body, Body-HTML, Quote-Note-Ref-Optional, Reactions[], Replies[], Restacks[], Created-At, Sensitive-Flag).

  - `Chat_Room` (Room_ID, Publication-Ref, Name, Description, Visibility {paid / founding / all-subscribers}, Members[]).

  - `Reader_App_Subscriber` (Reader_ID, Substack-Account-Email, Subscriptions[Publication-Refs[]], Inbox-Preferences, Notifications-Preferences).

- **Vendor primary APIs and endpoint shapes**:
  - Substack does NOT publish a stable public REST API for third-party developers. Known surfaces:
    - **RSS Feeds**: `https://<sub>.substack.com/feed` for newsletter posts; `/api/v1/podcast/feed/<id>` for podcast.
    - **Sitemap**: `https://<sub>.substack.com/sitemap.xml`.
    - **Unofficial JSON endpoints**: `https://<sub>.substack.com/api/v1/posts/<slug>` returns post JSON.
    - **OAuth-via-Substack**: limited Reader-App-side identity flow (Sign-in-with-Substack).
  - Auth: Stripe Standard handshake for payments; Substack-managed Stripe account on writer's behalf.
  - Imports: CSV upload + Mailchimp/Beehiiv/ConvertKit/Ghost/WordPress JSON imports.
  - Exports: CSV export of subscribers + Stripe-Subscription dashboard.
  - Webhooks: not exposed publicly.
  - SDKs: none official; community wrappers scrape HTML + RSS + unofficial JSON endpoints.

- **Vendor distinctive UX surfaces**:
  - "Substack Dashboard" — posts + subscribers + revenue + stats.
  - "Post Editor" — rich-text with paywall + audio + video + poll + image-block.
  - "Notes Feed" — Twitter-like microblog in Substack mobile app + web.
  - "Chat Rooms" — Discord-like chat for paid subscribers.
  - "Recommendations Page" — cross-publication subscribe-to-others.
  - "Bestseller Badge" — earned at subscriber-count thresholds.
  - "Reader Inbox" — unified inbox across all subscribed publications.
  - "Stripe-Backed Subscribe Modal" — checkout for paid subscriptions.
  - "Imports Wizard" — Mailchimp / Beehiiv / ConvertKit / Ghost / WordPress / CSV.
  - "Export Subscribers CSV" — writer self-service export.
  - "Substack Reads" — curated discovery surface.
  - "Substack Pro Dashboard" — advance/grant + dedicated CSM (top writers only).

  ```
    principal.role in resource.allowed_roles &&
    (resource.kind != "post_delete_paid_published" || (principal.role in ["owner"] && context.dual_control_approver_present == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "post_publish_paywalled" || principal.role in ["owner", "editor"]) &&
    (resource.kind != "plan_price_change_existing" || (principal.role == "owner" && context.dual_control_approver_present == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "subscriber_export_gdpr" || (principal.role == "owner" && context.gdpr_export_approved == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "subscriber_comp_grant_bulk" || (principal.role == "owner" && context.bulk_comp_approved == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "recommendation_add_cross_publication" || principal.role in ["owner", "editor"]) &&
    (resource.kind != "note_post_sensitive" || principal.role in ["owner"]) &&
    (resource.kind != "email_send_>100000" || (principal.role == "owner" && context.send_volume_approved == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "import_from_external" || (principal.role == "owner" && context.import_audit_consent == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "stripe_connect" || (principal.role == "owner" && context.stripe_kyc_complete == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "custom_domain_bind" || (principal.role == "owner" && context.dns_proof_provided == true)) &&
    (resource.kind != "bestseller_badge_issue" || (principal.role == "substack_employee" && context.thresholds_verified == true))
  };
  ```
  Per-jurisdiction packs: GDPR + KR-PIPA + EU-DPF (Subscriber export DSAR); CCPA + CPRA; CAN-SPAM (unsubscribe + sender-identification); CASL (Canada anti-spam consent); PCI-DSS (Stripe Standard); state-tax via Stripe Tax for paid subscriptions.

- **Ontology projection**:
  - `substack.publication` → `oya-web-publication-site`.
  - `substack.author` → `oya-iam-author` (Substack-Pro-flag + bestseller-badge-level preserved).
  - `substack.post` → `oya-web-post` (Type taxonomy + audience-tier-binding preserved).

  - `substack.note` + `substack.note_reaction` + `substack.restack` → `oya-collaboration-microblog-post` + `-reaction` + `-restack`.
  - `substack.chat_room` + `substack.chat_message` → `oya-collaboration-channel` + `-message` (paid-only access preserved).
  - `substack.comment` → `oya-collaboration-comment`.
  - `substack.discussion_thread` + `substack.poll` → `oya-collaboration-thread` + `oya-collaboration-poll`.

- **Workflow steps for displacement journey** (13 numbered steps — note no public API, so largely import-side):
  1. Provision Oyatie tenant + `web` + `commerce` + `marketing` + `collaboration` + `compliance` µservices with Substack-feature-parity (Newsletters + Paid Subscriptions + Notes + Chat + Podcast + Video + Recommendations + Comments).
  2. Export Substack via UI-driven Subscriber-CSV export + Stripe-Subscription dashboard + Posts-RSS feed + Notes/Chat manual archive (HTML scrape of own publication's pages — within ToS for own data).
  3. For audio + video, export via writer's storage source (Substack hosts but writers retain content).
  4. Per-Publication: re-create with subdomain + custom-domain + branding + author preserved.
  5. Per-Post: re-create from RSS feed + UI scrape with body-HTML + paywall + audience-tier preserved.
  6. Per-Section: re-create with visibility (public / paid) preserved.
  7. Per-Subscriber: import via CSV; preserve status + plan + paying-since + lifetime-revenue.
  8. Per-Subscription-Plan: re-create with Stripe-Product migration via Stripe Standard → Oyatie Stripe Connect; subscription-pipe handoff with subscriber notice.
  9. Per-Recommendation: re-bind cross-publication network edges to Oyatie marketing µservice.
  10. Per-Note + Chat-Room + Chat-Message + Comment + Discussion-Thread + Poll: import-as-archive (no public API; UI-side scrape of own data).
  11. Per-Podcast-Item + Video-Item: re-host on Oyatie + update RSS-enclosure URL with 301-redirect.
  12. Per-Email-Delivery stats: archive historical opens + clicks; Stripe-Subscription cutover with email notice to subscribers about new sender domain.
  13. Decommission Substack publication after 30-day shadow + final newsletter announcing platform move; Stripe-handoff; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Failure modes** (13 specific failures):
  - No public REST API means migration is UI + RSS + CSV based: per-publication scraper-driven export with rate-limit + ToS-compliant pacing.
  - Stripe-Standard handoff (Substack's Stripe-→ writer's direct Stripe → Oyatie Connect): per-subscriber Stripe-Customer + Stripe-Subscription re-bind via Stripe API; subscription state must remain unbroken.
  - Subscriber preservation across email-sender-domain change: per-publication SPF + DKIM + DMARC re-warm + IP-reputation transfer.
  - Notes microblog data export limitation (Notes have no export tool): per-author Notes scrape from public profile + screenshot archive.
  - Chat Room data export limitation (Chat has no export): per-room manual archive from UI.
  - Recommendations network is Substack-internal; cross-Substack-to-cross-Oyatie network requires bilateral re-bind: per-recommendation edge re-establish with publisher consent.
  - Bestseller-Badge is Substack-internal recognition — not portable: per-author archive as static-badge-image only.
  - Substack Pro grant/advance contract: per-author legal handoff (typically tied to Substack contract — may forfeit Pro status).
  - Reader App Inbox cross-publication subscription: per-reader subscriber-pool re-collect with Oyatie Reader equivalent.
  - Custom-domain DNS A/AAAA/CNAME pointing to Substack edge: per-domain DNS swap to Oyatie edge.
  - 301-redirect from `<sub>.substack.com/*` → Oyatie URL: not natively supported (Substack URL fixed) → only writer's custom-domain redirect possible.
  - Podcast RSS-enclosure URL change: per-episode 301 + iTunes/Spotify directory update.
  - CAN-SPAM + CASL consent re-validation during sender-domain change: per-subscriber re-confirm.

- **Migration playbook outline** (10 numbered steps):
  1. Inventory via Subscriber-CSV export + Stripe dashboard + RSS feed + UI archive.
  2. Plan 30-day shadow with sender-domain warm-up + Stripe-handoff.
  3. Migrate publication + posts (RSS + UI scrape) + sections + comments + discussion-threads + polls.
  4. Migrate subscribers + subscription-plans + Stripe-→ Oyatie cutover.
  5. Migrate Notes + Chat (manual archive) + Podcast + Video re-host.
  6. Re-bind Recommendations + cross-publication network to Oyatie equivalent.
  7. Migrate custom-domain DNS + email sender (SPF/DKIM/DMARC re-issue).
  8. Send final newsletter on Substack announcing migration; opt-in re-collect for sender-domain.
  9. Re-establish GDPR / CCPA / CAN-SPAM / CASL / PCI attestations.
  10. Decommission Substack publication after 30-day shadow; Stripe-handoff; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Naming justification**: `web` + `commerce` + `marketing` + `collaboration` + `compliance` are canonical 12-layer enum entries per ADR-0105 (13-value canonical); `substack` + `substack-newsletters` + `substack-paid-subscriptions` + `substack-network` + `substack-notes` + `substack-chat` + `substack-podcast` + `substack-video` + `substack-recommendations` + `substack-bestsellers` + `substack-reads` + `substack-pro` + `substack-reader-app` are benchmark alias-only. The `web` µservice (per ADR-0131 per-microservice flat layout) is the canonical Substack-equivalent network-first newsletter surface, distinct from Ghost (D-122, OSS publisher + self-host) and Beehiiv (D-124, ad-monetization + newsletter-network).

(See §27 of `docs/architecture/wave-3-g-synthesis-adjudication-2026-05-21.md` for synthesis-audit-blessed pattern.)

### Section D-124 - Beehiiv
- Vendor name and category: Beehiiv Inc. — beehiiv newsletter publishing platform: beehiiv Editor (rich-text + drag-drop blocks + image + video + audio + poll + signup-card + button + bookmark + embed + table + product + breakout + section-divider) + beehiiv Audience (subscribers + segments + tags + custom-fields + GDPR-compliant import) + beehiiv Ad Network (top sponsorship marketplace — Direct + Boosts + Ad-Network) + beehiiv Boosts (paid subscriber-acquisition — pay-other-newsletters to recommend you, marketplace-based) + Recommendations (free cross-newsletter recommendations) + beehiiv Polls + beehiiv Surveys + beehiiv Premium Subscriptions (Stripe-based paid tiers + Founding Member + comp + free trials) + Custom Domain + Custom Landing Pages + beehiiv Workspaces (multi-publication teams + roles + permissions) + beehiiv API (public REST API — unlike Substack, beehiiv exposes documented REST API) + beehiiv Webhooks + beehiiv Magic Links + beehiiv Referral Program (built-in referral tracking + rewards + leaderboard) + beehiiv Segments (rule-based + saved) + beehiiv AI (AI Writer + AI Translate + AI Edit + AI Title Generator) + beehiiv Analytics (3D Analytics — opens + clicks + revenue) + beehiiv Forms (signup forms + popups + inline) + beehiiv Embed (web-embed signup) + beehiiv Workspace SSO (Enterprise).
- Coverage tier: A (capability fit on `web` (newsletter publication — beehiiv differentiated by ad-network monetization + Boosts + public REST API + workspaces multi-publication) + `commerce` (Premium Subscriptions via Stripe + Boosts marketplace) + `marketing` (Audience + Segments + Recommendations + Boosts + Referral Program + AI Writer) + `intelligence` (beehiiv AI Writer + Translate + Edit + Title Generator) + `apigw` (beehiiv Public REST API v2 + Webhooks) + `developer-sdk` (REST API + Magic Links + Embeds + Forms) + `compliance` (SOC-2 + GDPR + CCPA + CAN-SPAM + CASL + PCI-DSS via Stripe + EU-AI-Act for AI features) + `marketplace` (Ad Network + Boosts marketplace + Recommendations network)). Capability-tier mapping per ADR-0316: Launch (Free up to 2500 subs) → **Silver**; Scale → **Gold**; Max + Enterprise (SSO + advanced-roles + custom-billing + dedicated-CSM + Workspaces multi-publication + Premium Subscriptions + advanced analytics + 99.9%-SLA + AI Premium) → **Platinum**.
- Oyatie destination: `web` (newsletter publication anchor); `commerce` (Premium Subs + Boosts marketplace); `marketing` (Audience + Segments + Recommendations + Referral); `intelligence` (beehiiv AI); `apigw` (REST v2 + Webhooks); `developer-sdk` (Magic Links + Embeds + Forms); `compliance` (SOC-2 + GDPR + CAN-SPAM + PCI + EU-AI-Act); `marketplace` (Ad Network + Boosts).

- **Failure modes** (13 specific failures):
  - Segment filter-expression DSL drift (beehiiv segment-rules are publication-specific DSL): per-segment rule transpile + count compare.
  - Source-provenance taxonomy (direct / signup_form / recommendation / boost / referral / api / import / migration): per-subscriber source preserve.
  - Post audience-tier dual-content (Content-Free-HTML + Content-Premium-HTML): per-post both variants preserve.

  - Referral attribution chain (referrer-subscriber → referred-subscriber): per-edge preserve + recompute counts.
  - Magic-Link secret rotation during cutover: per-link cryptographic re-issue with new HMAC key.
  - Sender-domain change for email-delivery (SPF + DKIM + DMARC): per-publication sender-warm-up + reputation transfer.
  - Custom-Hostname DNS swap (A/AAAA + CNAME from beehiiv-edge to Oyatie-edge): per-publication DNS coordination.
  - AI Writer + Translate + Edit + Title-Generator opt-in re-collect (EU-AI-Act): per-publication AI-policy ledger.
  - Workspaces SSO + multi-publication permissions schema drift: per-workspace SSO IdP re-bind + role map preserve.

  3. Migrate workspaces + publications + posts + subscribers + tags + custom-fields + segments.
  4. Migrate premium-plans + premium-subscriptions + Stripe-cutover.
  5. Migrate ad-network campaigns + boost-offers + recommendations + referral programs.
  6. Migrate polls + surveys + forms + magic-links + webhooks.
  7. Migrate beehiiv-AI action-log as conformance ledger.
  8. DNS swap custom-hostname; sender-domain SPF/DKIM/DMARC re-issue.
  9. Re-establish SOC-2 / GDPR / CCPA / CAN-SPAM / CASL / PCI / EU-AI-Act attestations.
  10. Decommission beehiiv per-publication after 30-day shadow; beehiiv contract sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Naming justification**: `web` + `commerce` + `marketing` + `intelligence` + `apigw` + `developer-sdk` + `compliance` + `marketplace` are canonical 12-layer enum entries per ADR-0105 (13-value canonical); `beehiiv` + `beehiiv-audience` + `beehiiv-ad-network` + `beehiiv-boosts` + `beehiiv-recommendations` + `beehiiv-referral-program` + `beehiiv-premium-subscriptions` + `beehiiv-polls` + `beehiiv-surveys` + `beehiiv-magic-links` + `beehiiv-workspaces` + `beehiiv-ai` + `beehiiv-3d-analytics` are benchmark alias-only. The `web` µservice (per ADR-0131 per-microservice flat layout) is the canonical beehiiv-equivalent ad-monetized + boosts-marketplace newsletter surface, distinct from Substack (D-123, network-first paid-only) and Ghost (D-122, OSS + self-host).

  ```
    (resource.kind != "project_delete" || (principal.role in ["project_lead", "org_admin"] && context.dual_control_approver_present == true)) &&

    (resource.kind != "comment_delete_other" || principal.role in ["team_admin", "org_admin"]) &&
  ```

  - GitHub PR + commit auto-link: per-issue GitHub-link integration re-establish.
  - Slack integration channel-binding for Triage + Customer-Requests: per-team Slack OAuth re-grant + channel-map preserve.
  - Customer Request source-binding (Front / Intercom / Zendesk / Salesforce): per-source integration re-grant.

  - Linear AI Agents Platform agent-action mutation-grant: per-agent action-scope preserve + re-grant.

### Section D-154 - PlanetScale
- Vendor name and category: PlanetScale (PlanetScale, Inc.) — Managed MySQL-compatible serverless database built on Vitess: Databases + Branches (Git-style schema branching) + Deploy Requests (schema deployment PRs) + Schema Snapshots + Connection Strings (per-branch + per-password) + Insights (query performance + index suggestions) + Boost (managed Vitess query caching) + Safe Migrations (online DDL via gh-ost) + Foreign Key Constraints (limited) + Vector indexing (preview) + PlanetScale CLI (`pscale`) + REST API + Terraform provider + AWS / GCP regions + PlanetScale (logical replication CDC to Snowflake/BigQuery via Singer + ETL partners) + Workflow rollback + Audit Log + SSO (SAML for Scaler Pro+) + IP Allowlist + AWS PrivateLink (Enterprise) + Customer-Managed-Keys (Enterprise) + Multi-region + Backup (daily snapshots + PITR) + Read-only regions (replicas) + Scaler / Scaler Pro / Enterprise tiers.
- Coverage tier: A (capability fit on `data` (MySQL-compatible databases + branches + schemas + replicas + backup) + `developer-experience` (branches + deploy requests + schema snapshots + CLI + Terraform) + `intelligence` (Insights + Boost cache) + `apigw` (per-branch connection strings) + `identity` (SSO + SAML + RBAC) + `network` (PrivateLink + IP allowlist) + `compliance` (SOC-2 + HIPAA-eligible + CMK)). Capability-tier mapping per ADR-0316: Hobby → **Silver**; Scaler / Scaler Pro → **Gold**; Enterprise (SSO + PrivateLink + CMK + HIPAA-BAA + dedicated-support + 99.999%-SLA + custom-region) → **Platinum**.
- Oyatie destination: `data` (databases + branches + replicas + backup anchor); `developer-experience` (branches + deploy-requests + schema-snapshots); `intelligence` (Insights + Boost); `apigw` (per-branch connection-strings); `identity` (SSO + SAML); `network` (PrivateLink + IP-allowlist); `compliance` (SOC-2 + HIPAA + CMK).

- **Vendor primary APIs and endpoint shapes**:
  - REST API v1: `https://api.planetscale.com/v1/` shapes `organizations/{org}` + `organizations/{org}/databases` + `organizations/{org}/databases/{db}/branches` + `organizations/{org}/databases/{db}/branches/{br}/schema` + `organizations/{org}/databases/{db}/deploy-requests` + `organizations/{org}/databases/{db}/branches/{br}/passwords` + `organizations/{org}/databases/{db}/branches/{br}/backups` + `organizations/{org}/databases/{db}/branches/{br}/restores` + `organizations/{org}/databases/{db}/branches/{br}/insights` + `organizations/{org}/audit-log`.
  - MySQL wire protocol: `<host>.<region>.psdb.cloud:3306` with TLS-required + SCRAM-style PSK via Password.
  - CLI: `pscale` (org switch + database create/list + branch create/promote/diff + deploy-request create/approve/queue + password create + backup create + restore create + connect / shell + insights queries / index-suggestions + boost queries / enable + audit-log list).
  - Terraform provider: `planetscale/planetscale` (`planetscale_database` + `planetscale_branch` + `planetscale_password` + `planetscale_deploy_request` + `planetscale_organization_member`).
  - PlanetScale (CDC): WebSocket + change-stream endpoint with PSK auth (logical replication via Vitess VStream).

- **Vendor distinctive UX surfaces**:
  - "Branches" — production + development + (optional) sandbox branches per database.
  - "Deploy Requests" — schema-change-as-PR with approvals + queue + auto-cutover.
  - "Schema Diff Viewer" — visual DDL diff with conflict markers.
  - "Insights" — slow query + most-active query + index suggestion dashboards.
  - "Boost" — managed-cache toggle per-query with TTL + hit-rate UX.
  - "Backups + Restores" — per-branch snapshot + cross-branch restore.
  - "Console (in-browser SQL)" — read-only on production, full on dev branches.
  - "PlanetScale Connect" — outbound CDC to data warehouse partners.
  - "Schema Snapshots" — point-in-time schema captures.
  - "Production Branch Promotion" — safe-migrations + lock-mode promotion.
  - "Cluster Sizing" — `pscale_cluster` size selector PS-10 through PS-400.
  - "Multi-region Replicas" — read-only replicas in additional regions.
  - "PrivateLink" — Enterprise private connectivity (AWS).

- **Workflow steps for displacement journey** (15 numbered steps):
  1. Provision Oyatie tenant + `data` + `developer-experience` + `intelligence` + `apigw` + `identity` + `network` + `compliance` µservices with PlanetScale-feature-parity.
  2. Export PlanetScale org + databases + branches + schemas + deploy-requests + passwords + backups + insights + boost + audit-log via REST API + CLI.
  3. Plan per-database migration cohorts (group by region + cluster-size).
  4. Per-Database: re-create with region + cluster-size + default-branch preserved.
  5. Per-Branch: re-create with parent-branch + production-flag + safe-migrations + region preserved.
  6. Per-Schema-Snapshot: import DDL dump as Oyatie schema-snapshot.
  7. Per-Deploy-Request: import DDL + state-machine + approvals (replay for audit chain).
  8. Per-Password: re-issue with role + region + TTL preserved; rotate client connection strings.
  9. Per-Backup: import + register with retention preserved.
  10. Per-Insights-Query + Index-Suggestion: import as observability + intelligence baseline.
  11. Per-Boost-Query: re-enable with TTL preserved.
  12. Per-Read-Only-Region + PrivateLink + IP-Allowlist + CMK: re-establish.
  13. Per-PlanetScale-Connect-Subscription: re-establish CDC to Oyatie data µservice / partner DWH.
  14. Per-Audit-Event + SSO: import audit chain + re-establish federation.
  15. Decommission PlanetScale per-database after 30-day shadow + CDC-tail cutover; PlanetScale sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Failure modes** (16 specific failures):
  - Vitess sharding semantics (vindex + keyspace + scatter queries): per-keyspace shard-plan preserve.
  - Foreign-key support gap (PlanetScale has limited FK support): per-schema FK-policy alignment + application-level constraint shim.
  - Online DDL gh-ost semantics (cutover window + lock window): per-deploy operation timing preserve.
  - Deploy-request state-machine (open / queued / in_progress / ready / closed / cancelled / errored): per-DR state-replay.
  - Branch-promotion semantics (dev → production safe-migrations lock): per-branch promotion-policy preserve.
  - Insights query normalization (Vitess plan vs Oyatie plan): per-query normalized-form preserve.
  - Boost cache key + TTL + invalidation semantics: per-query cache-policy preserve.
  - Per-password region pin (primary vs replica) + TLS CA chain: per-password region + cert preserve.
  - Backup encryption + per-branch retention-days: per-backup retention preserve.
  - PlanetScale (VStream) resume-token compatibility: per-subscription tail preserve.
  - Cluster-size step taxonomy (PS-10..PS-400): per-database sizing-mapping.
  - Production-branch read-only web-console invariant: per-branch console-policy preserve.
  - Audit-log retention (Enterprise 365-day): per-stream retention preserve.
  - PrivateLink endpoint-service-name drift: per-attachment re-bind.
  - CMK key-policy / grants: per-binding policy migrate.
  - SSO group-mapping → role assignment drift: per-mapping table preserve.

- **Migration playbook outline** (10 numbered steps):
  1. Inventory via PlanetScale REST + CLI + audit-log.
  2. Plan 30-day shadow with PlanetScale-(VStream) dual-write to Oyatie.
  3. Migrate databases + branches + schemas + deploy-requests + schema-snapshots.
  4. Migrate passwords + backups + insights + boost.
  5. Migrate audit-log + SSO + IP-allowlist + PrivateLink + CMK + read-only regions.
  6. Re-establish FK + DDL conventions + online-migration tooling parity.
  7. Re-establish SOC-2 + ISO + GDPR + HIPAA + EU-DPF attestations.
  8. Cut MySQL connection strings + DNS to Oyatie endpoint; preserve `psdb.cloud` alias.
  9. Re-establish PlanetScale-CDC equivalents.
  10. Decommission PlanetScale per-database after 30-day shadow + CDC-tail-zero sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Naming justification**: `data` + `developer-experience` + `intelligence` + `apigw` + `identity` + `network` + `compliance` are canonical 12-layer enum entries per ADR-0105 (13-value canonical); `planetscale` + `pscale` + `planetscale-branches` + `planetscale-deploy-requests` + `planetscale-boost` + `planetscale-insights` + `planetscale-connect` + `planetscale-private-link` + `planetscale-cmk` + `planetscale-schema-snapshots` are benchmark alias-only. The `data` µservice (per ADR-0131 per-microservice flat layout) is the canonical PlanetScale-equivalent managed-MySQL-on-Vitess surface.

### Section D-155 - Neon
- Vendor name and category: Neon (Neon, Inc., recently Databricks-acquired) — Serverless Postgres with storage-compute separation: Projects + Branches (copy-on-write Postgres branches via storage decoupling) + Compute Endpoints (autosuspend + autoscale + read replicas) + Bucardo logical replication + Neon Auth (formerly Stack Auth) + Neon RLS Authorize (JWT-based pg-rbac) + Vector (pgvector preinstalled) + AI gateway integrations + Time-travel (PITR up to 30 days) + Restore branch from any point-in-time + Neon Local (local dev replica) + Neon Proxy (SQL-over-HTTP + WebSocket) + Drizzle / Prisma adapters + Branch APIs (Vercel + GitHub PR preview integrations) + IP allow + Audit Log + AWS + GCP + Azure (preview) regions + SOC-2 + HIPAA-eligible + Free / Launch / Scale / Business + Enterprise.
- Coverage tier: A (capability fit on `data` (Postgres + pgvector + branches + read replicas + PITR) + `developer-experience` (branches + branch-per-PR + Drizzle/Prisma adapters + Neon Local + GitHub integration) + `intelligence` (pgvector + AI gateway) + `identity` (Neon Auth + Neon RLS Authorize) + `apigw` (Neon Proxy SQL-over-HTTP + WebSocket) + `compliance` (SOC-2 + HIPAA-eligible)). Capability-tier mapping per ADR-0316: Free / Launch → **Silver**; Scale / Business → **Gold**; Enterprise (HIPAA-BAA + PrivateLink + SSO + CMK + 99.99%-SLA + dedicated-support) → **Platinum**.
- Oyatie destination: `data` (Postgres + pgvector + branches + replicas anchor); `developer-experience` (branches + branch-per-PR + adapters); `intelligence` (pgvector + AI gateway); `identity` (Neon Auth + RLS Authorize); `apigw` (Neon Proxy); `compliance` (SOC-2 + HIPAA).

  11. Per-Vector-Index: re-create with type (ivfflat/hnsw) + distance + parameters preserved; re-embed.
  12. Per-Neon-Auth-Project + Auth-User: re-create OAuth providers + import users via SCIM.
  13. Per-Integration: re-establish Vercel / GitHub / Drizzle / Prisma / LangChain / Stack-Auth / Clerk-Auth bindings.
  14. Per-IP-Allowlist + CMK + SSO + Audit-Stream: re-establish.
  15. Decommission Neon per-project after 30-day shadow + logical-replication-tail cutover; Neon sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Failure modes** (16 specific failures):
  - Copy-on-write storage semantics (Neon page-server + safekeeper) vs Oyatie storage substrate: per-branch CoW alias preserve.
  - Parent-LSN + Parent-Timestamp branch fork point: per-branch fork-anchor preserve.
  - Compute autosuspend semantics (timeout + cold-start latency): per-endpoint suspend-policy preserve.
  - Autoscale CU range (min/max compute units) semantics: per-endpoint scaling-policy preserve.
  - pgvector index type (ivfflat / hnsw) + distance taxonomy + parameters: per-index re-build + recall test.
  - Postgres extension catalog (pgvector + plpgsql + uuid-ossp + citext + ...): per-DB extension-set preserve.
  - JWT-based RLS Authorize semantics (`auth.user_id()` etc.): per-DB rls-helper functions preserve.
  - Neon Auth user metadata (client + server JSON): per-user metadata preserve.
  - Vercel / GitHub branch-per-PR integration secrets: per-integration re-grant.
  - Serverless driver (`@neondatabase/serverless` WS) compatibility on Oyatie edge: per-driver shim.
  - Neon Proxy SQL-over-HTTP authentication (API-key + request signing): per-project key rotation.
  - Read-replica endpoint vs primary endpoint connection-string semantics: per-branch endpoint-set preserve.
  - History-retention-seconds (Free 24h / Scale 7d / Business 30d): per-project retention preserve.
  - Branch CPU-usage-seconds metering (free tier compute-hours): per-branch usage continuity.
  - Audit-log retention + format: per-stream retention preserve.
  - IP-allowlist enforcement semantics + CIDR aggregation: per-project allowlist-set preserve.

- **Migration playbook outline** (10 numbered steps):
  1. Inventory via Neon REST + neonctl + audit-log.
  2. Plan 30-day shadow with logical replication (`pglogical` / native `pub-sub`) to Oyatie.
  3. Migrate projects + branches + endpoints + roles + databases.
  4. Migrate snapshots + JWKS + vector-indexes + integrations.
  5. Migrate Neon Auth projects + users + IP-allowlist + CMK + SSO.
  6. Re-establish pgvector + pg extensions parity.
  7. Re-establish RLS Authorize JWT helpers.
  8. Re-establish SOC-2 + ISO + GDPR + HIPAA + EU-DPF attestations.
  9. Cut Postgres connection strings + DNS to Oyatie endpoint; preserve `neon.tech` alias.
  10. Decommission Neon per-project after 30-day shadow + logical-replication-lag-zero sunset; tenant ledger evidence per ADR-0247 + ADR-0250 + ADR-0251 §D-10.

- **Naming justification**: `data` + `developer-experience` + `intelligence` + `identity` + `apigw` + `compliance` are canonical 12-layer enum entries per ADR-0105 (13-value canonical); `neon` + `neon-branches` + `neon-endpoints` + `neon-auth` + `neon-rls-authorize` + `neon-proxy` + `neon-serverless-driver` + `neon-local` + `neonctl` + `neon-vercel-integration` + `neon-github-integration` are benchmark alias-only. The `data` µservice (per ADR-0131 per-microservice flat layout) is the canonical Neon-equivalent serverless-Postgres-with-branching surface.

### Section D-136 - Netlify

- **Vendor distinctive UX surfaces**:

  - "Netlify Connect" data-source sync and GraphQL content layer console.

- **Cedar permit shape**:
  ```cedar
  permit(
    principal == Oyatie::User::"<netlify-user-id>",
    action in [
      Oyatie::Action::"NetlifySiteCreate", Oyatie::Action::"NetlifySiteDelete",
      Oyatie::Action::"NetlifySiteUpdate", Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyDeployCreate",
      Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyDeployPublish", Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyDeployLock",
      Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyBuildCancel", Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyBuildHookTrigger",
      Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyEnvVarRead", Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyEnvVarWrite",
      Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyFunctionInvoke", Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyFunctionLogRead",
      Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyEdgeFunctionBind", Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyFormRead",
      Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyFormSubmissionDelete", Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyDomainBind",
      Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyDNSRecordWrite", Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyCertificateIssue",
      Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyRedirectEdit", Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyHeaderEdit",
      Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyPluginInstall", Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyWebhookManage",
      Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyAnalyticsRead", Oyatie::Action::"NetlifyConnectSourceBind"
    ],
    resource in [
      Oyatie::Resource::NetlifyTeam::"<team-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::NetlifySite::"<site-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::NetlifyDeploy::"<deploy-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::NetlifyFunction::"<function-name>",
      Oyatie::Resource::NetlifyForm::"<form-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::NetlifyDomain::"<domain>",
      Oyatie::Resource::NetlifyDNSZone::"<zone-id>",
      Oyatie::Resource::NetlifyEnvVar::"<key>",
      Oyatie::Resource::NetlifyWebhook::"<hook-id>",
  ```
